summary: Bunzai treats imported regex patterns as untrusted data and combines conservative structural admission with bounded allocation. Native matching is synchronous, so a between-match clock cannot interrupt one RegExp call. The parser and shared AST analyzer refuse unsupported syntax and suspicious or dangerous repetition shapes, including sequential ambiguity, bounded nested loops and caseless alternatives. Source length and capture counts are bounded. Runtime validates the pattern after macro substitution, caps projected replacement and macro output during construction, bounds match enumeration and retained trace spans, and reports refusal without partial output from the failing rule. Studio execution adds a disposable worker with request, batch and output limits plus termination; static Pages refuses previews that cannot provide isolation. Tests cover demonstrated attack families and preserve safe controls. These checks are logical defenses with unit and source evidence, not a complete regex-runtime bound or proof of packaged WebView isolation, browser behavior or native-library security. Direct Kit and lore or Skill callers still lack preemption inside a native match.

sections.title: Structural admission
sections.summary: The shared validateRule and vetPattern owners require structurally readable Unicode-compatible syntax, with no heuristic fallback for unsupported patterns. Source patterns and replacements cap at ten thousand characters and captures at 128. The AST screen covers nested variable repetitions, overlapping alternatives, repeated backreferences and sequential overlapping repetition, including bounded variants, single-branch groups, nullable seams and conservative case folding. Execution refuses suspicious and dangerous reports, while mandatory disjoint separators preserve accepted controls. Character-set reasoning remains approximate: acceptance is not proof of linear time, and conservative rejection can include harmless patterns. Complexity scores explain patterns rather than replacing structural admission.

sections.title: Runtime and allocation boundaries
sections.summary: Runtime validates the find pattern after macro substitution so variable values cannot bypass admission. Unresolved templates may fail static health checks until runtime context supplies them. Shared regex limits bound text construction and retained changed outputs to one million UTF-16 units, projected macro substitutions, replacement fragments, actual case expansion and prospective full results before concatenation. A limit leaves the failing rule unchanged and explicitly skips later rules, preserving earlier completed work. Enumeration stops at the first requested match or the thousand-match ceiling plus one, and retained capture spans cap at one hundred thousand across a set. Worker single requests cap at two hundred thousand characters, batches at one million input and output characters, five hundred rules and three hundred items. Worker termination supplements these logical allocation limits, which are not measured physical-memory guarantees.

sections.title: Evidence and remaining limits
sections.summary: Tests exercise the demonstrated polynomial pattern, grouped and bounded repetitions, caseless alternatives, unsupported-parser bypasses and macro-substituted patterns, alongside accepted safe controls and built-in templates. Allocation regressions use bounded probes rather than destructive host payloads. Source validators and worker boundaries have test evidence, but this audit does not prove packaged isolation, browser compatibility or complete regex safety. Direct core callers, including Kit draft tools and lore or Skill trigger matching, cannot preempt an individual native match. Rejections appear as traces and plain Health or inspector errors; culprit spans are returned without new highlighting UI.
